title: The Homes We Leave Behind
structure: One episode with three internal movements

movements.title: The Distance Starts Here
movements.purpose: Begin with departure, homesickness, exile, and the ordinary things that become emotionally enormous when home is far away.

sections.purpose: Open on the moment a familiar home becomes a place one can only visit, then widen into longing for country, landscape, family, and a life interrupted.
Contrast dramatic exile with the mundane freedoms, landscapes, objects, and relationships that distance makes newly precious.

movements.ending_handoff: Distance turns the remembered home into a destination, but arrival does not guarantee recognition.

movements.title: You Can Go Back—But to What?
movements.purpose: Center the anchor story and compare returns to houses, towns, landscapes, graves, family, and civic places transformed by time.

sections.purpose: Center the Appalachian anchor story, then echo it through a decaying house, an ancestral landscape, and a native land transformed over twenty years.
Walk through cemeteries, courthouse squares, civic change, divided urban identity, and a gated lyric fragment to ask who owns a remembered place.

movements.ending_handoff: When the place no longer matches the memory, people find other containers for belonging.

movements.title: What the Web Remembered
movements.purpose: Explore sensory nostalgia, inherited local memory, friendship, art, naming, and the strange partial record left by old web captures.

sections.purpose: Move from sensory and false nostalgia into inherited town history, pioneer memory, and a landscape that became lovable only after leaving it.
Close through friendship, seasonal ritual, an intimate poem, and a company named for a childhood park—containers that keep belonging present while the archive remains partial.

movements.ending_handoff: Close on the idea that an archive can preserve evidence of longing without restoring the home, person, page, or context that produced it.
